edge.title: The machine that didn't work the first time
edge.setup: At a fuel pump or a small restaurant: your card is taken out of sight, or the POS machine 'fails' and needs a second swipe, or the ATM card slot looks slightly proud of the panel. The failed transaction is the part worth noticing.
edge.tell: Your card leaving your sight, or a swipe that mysteriously needs doing twice.
move: Never let the card leave your hand — carry it to the machine, or ask the machine to come to you.
Tap beats dip beats swipe. The magnetic stripe is the only part that can be cloned wholesale.
Tug the ATM card slot before inserting; skimmers are overlays and they move. Cover the keypad with your other hand regardless of who's around.
Turn on transaction alerts for every amount, not just large ones — test transactions are small on purpose.
edge.why: Cloning needs two things: the stripe data and the PIN. The 'failed' swipe captures the first; the camera or overlay captures the second. Defeating either half defeats the attack, which is why keeping the card in view is disproportionately effective.
edge.variants: Same shape: a waiter 'who'll bring the machine' and returns slowly, free-Wi-Fi payment pages, QR codes pasted over the shop's real one.

lens.name: Moral hazard
lens.one_line: People take more risk when someone else carries the downside.
lens.detail: Insurance against theft reduces the care taken to prevent theft. Bailouts reduce the caution of the next lender. Deductibles, co-pays and skin-in-the-game rules exist specifically to re-link a decision to its consequence — which is why their removal, however humane it sounds, changes behaviour.
elsewhere: Limited liability encourages risk-taking — deliberately, as a feature.
A free replacement warranty subtly reduces how carefully a device is handled.
Deposit guarantees reduce depositors' scrutiny of their bank.
lens.test: Who eats the loss if this goes wrong? Whoever it is, their caution is the only caution in the system.
lens.today: The Pink Line's elevated stretch still awaits CMRS safety clearance, with BMRCL due to respond to the inspection observations next week, while the CM has already sought a date from the PM to open it (Deccan Herald, The Hindu). Whoever announces an opening collects the credit; the commuter carries the cost of any shortcut. That gap is why the independent clearance matters, and why a fixed date before it is signed off deserves a raised eyebrow.

moved.what: BMRCL is due to respond next week to observations from the Commissioner of Railway Safety on the Pink Line, and no opening date is fixed (The Hindu, Deccan Herald).
moved.so_what: Do not plan a move, a lease or a commute around the Pink Line opening this month. Treat the first date you hear as provisional until the safety clearance is reported.

moved.what: A long-neglected Bengaluru road got an overnight fix after public outcry, while East Bengaluru parents have petitioned over '2 hours for 2 km' commutes and road repairs (Times of India, Moneycontrol).
moved.so_what: Public, specific complaints with photos and a location appear to move repairs faster than private ones. If a stretch on your route is bad, post it publicly and tag the civic body.

moved.what: The Karnataka High Court has held that the Registrar of Societies should not adjudicate private disputes between members or rival groups that need civil rights decided (Times of India).
moved.so_what: If your resident or housing society is in a dispute with a rival group, a Registrar complaint may not settle it; expect to need a civil court. Keep minutes, notices and receipts organised now.

moved.what: The Sensex closed 1,100 points higher today, adding about Rs 4 trillion to investor wealth (NDTV).
moved.so_what: One strong day changes nothing about your plan. Do not chase it or change SIPs on a single session.

carry_over.prompt: A caller from 'your bank' knows your name, your card's last four digits and a recent restaurant spend, then says an OTP is on its way for verification. What is the one rule that settles it?
carry_over.answer: Anyone asking you to read out a code is, by definition, not your bank.

quiz.question: At a pump or restaurant, the card machine 'fails' and asks for a second swipe. What is the safest move?
options: Give the card to the staff to retry inside
Stop, keep the card in hand and pay by tap or UPI
Share the PIN so they can help
quiz.why: A failed swipe can capture stripe data; keeping the card in sight and using tap defeats the attack.
